    AI Overview
    A great contact form balances gathering the information your team needs to respond effectively with minimizing friction for the user. Limit your form to 3–5 core fields (Name, Email, Message), use a single-column layout, and only make truly critical fields required to prevent users from abandoning the page. 
    Ensure your contact form is fully optimized by reviewing this checklist: 
    🎯 Essential Fields
    • Name: Combine first and last names into a single field.
    • Email Address: Essential for replying. Ensure you have a formatting validation rule in place.
    • Message Box: A large text area for the user to explain their needs.
    • Phone Number: Optional. Only include if your business strictly requires calling leads.
    • Inquiry Dropdown: Optional. A simple dropdown (e.g., "Sales", "Support", "General") helps route submissions to the right team member. 
    ⚙️ Usability & UX
    • Single-Column Layout: Avoid multi-column layouts, as they confuse reading flow on mobile devices.
    • Clear Labels: Place labels above the input fields, not just inside them as disappearing placeholder text.
    • Visible Submit Button: Use a contrasting color and clear action text like "Send Message" rather than "Submit". 
    🔒 Security & Privacy
    • Spam Protection: Protect your inbox by integrating Google reCAPTCHA or a similar anti-spam tool.
    • Consent Checkbox: If you add a newsletter sign-up, include an unchecked, optional consent checkbox to comply with privacy laws. 
    📬 Testing & Post-Submission
    • Test Submissions: Send a test message through the form on both desktop and mobile to ensure it delivers correctly.
    • Auto-Responder: Set up an automated email that acknowledges receipt of their message and outlines what to expect next.
    • Thank You Page: Redirect the user to a dedicated "Thank You" page to confirm their message went through. 
    If you would like, let me know:
    • What content management system or website builder you are using (e.g., WordPress, Wix, Squarespace)
    • The main purpose of your contact form (e.g., lead generation, customer support, booking)

    What should a contact form include?
    Good contact forms are simple, mobile-friendly, and only ask for essential information like name, email, and a message or specific inquiry. The best examples include clear labels, helpful placeholder text, a strong call-to-action button, and minimal required fields to reduce friction and increase conversions.
